title: Can we list all the prime numbers from 1 to 100?
description: A table of the numbers from one to a hundred is sieved by circling and crossing out, and the circled numbers are the primes. Keeko doubts the first step and says that one is a prime number.
teaching_notes: One idea: circle the next number that is left and cross out all its later multiples, and what stays circled is prime. Watch for students who keep one as a prime or who forget to cross out the multiples of every circled number.

source: Can we list all the prime numbers from 1 to 100? Follow the
video_script.why: The child follows the circling and crossing out on the table from one to a hundred and sees that the circled numbers are the primes.
video_script.substitution: Circle the next uncrossed number and cross out its later multiples, and repeat.
video_script.anchor: The table of the numbers from 1 to 100 in ten rows of ten
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko wants to circle one as a prime. One has only one factor, itself, and a prime must have exactly two factors, so one is crossed out.
video_script.payoff_line: The circled numbers are the primes, and there are twenty five of them up to one hundred.

final_answer.spoken: the circled numbers are the twenty five primes up to one hundred

maths_rules: 1 is crossed out first: it has one factor, so it is neither prime nor composite
2 is circled and its multiples 4, 6, 8 and so on are crossed out
3 is circled and 6, 9, 12 and so on are crossed out; 5 is circled and 10, 15, 20 and so on are crossed out; 7 is circled and 14, 21, 28 and so on are crossed out
91 = 7 × 13 is crossed out in the round of 7
from 21 to 30 only 23 and 29 stay circled
video_script.design: The ten by ten table fills with crossed out numbers in amber and circled numbers in teal as each round is done.

beats.on_screen: Circle = keep. Cross out = composite. A multiple of a smaller number has that number as a factor. The Sieve of Eratosthenes.

<bookmark mark='name'/>This way of finding primes is called the Sieve of Eratosthenes, after a Greek mathematician.
